title: A bar total is the colimit of its principal lower ideals
statement: Let I be a preorder and A a preadditive category with a zero object and coproducts in the universes of I and Nat. For D:I→CochainComplex(A,Int), the total bars of its restrictions to the principal lower ideals {i|i≤j}, with their inclusion maps, have colimit the full total bar [def-sc-preorder-bar-total]. Their terminal augmentations to D(j) form a natural transformation to D [lem-sc-preorder-bar-terminal-augmentation].

source.place: The source-bar, least-block unit contraction, and finite-cone-block paragraphs.

proof.text: A monotone finite string lies in the principal lower ideal of its last vertex. Given a cocone on the lower-ideal bars, define its map out of each full-bar generator using that last vertex. If the string also lies below j, cocone naturality identifies this map with the map from the j-th lower-ideal bar. Therefore the degreewise maps are well defined and satisfy every cocone equation. Commutation with differentials follows by testing on the lower-ideal generators, since their inclusions are chain maps and jointly generate. Coproduct extensionality proves uniqueness. Evaluation of complexes creates colimits, giving the stated universal property.
